I-IV-V.description: Classic primary triad progression (e.g., G -> C -> D); prevents tonic stickiness on I.

I-V6-vi.description: First-inversion bass walkdown (e.g., G -> D/F# -> Em, A -> E/G# -> F#m, C -> G/B -> Am).

I-I6-IV.description: Stepwise ascending bass bridge (e.g., G -> G/B -> C, C -> C/E -> F, D -> D/F# -> G).

chord_confusion_fixes.reason: When bass shifts to C2 with C-E-G triad notes after G, resolve to C despite shared G5 fifth/vocal overtone.
When bass shifts to D2 with D-F#-A triad notes, resolve to D major.
First-inversion G/B stepwise bass bridge between G and C.
First-inversion D/F# bass walkdown between G and Em.
First-inversion E/G# bass walkdown between A and F#m.
D pedal bass with suspended 4th G resolving back to D.

strumming_patterns.4/4_slow: D - D U - U D U (steady 8th-note acoustic groove with light palm-mute on beats 2 & 4)
strumming_patterns.4/4_mid: D - D U - U D U (folk/pop syncopated 8th-note groove; accent beats 2 and 4)
strumming_patterns.4/4_fast: D - D U D U D U (driving 8th/16th rhythm; keep wrist loose for rapid passing chords)
strumming_patterns.3/4_waltz: D - D U D U (waltz 3/4 feel: strong bass root on beat 1, light brush strums on beats 2 & 3)
strumming_patterns.6/8_compound: D - - D U D - - D U (compound 6/8 sway; accent beats 1 and 4)
strumming_patterns.fingerstyle_arpeggio: p - i - m - a - m - i (thumb 'p' alternates bass roots on strings 6/5/4 while i-m-a pluck treble strings 3-2-1)

playing_tip_rules.slash_walkdown: Emphasize the moving bass note on the lowest fretted string with your thumb or a firm down-pick so the stepwise slash-chord walkdown rings clearly.
playing_tip_rules.sus_filler: Keep your anchor fingers planted on the base triad while adding or lifting your pinky/index finger for the sus2/sus4 embellishment.
playing_tip_rules.soft_dynamics: Match the track's dynamic contour by strumming closer to the neck with lighter pick velocity during soft chord passages, then digging in near the bridge on main chorus chords.
playing_tip_rules.barre_transition: Pre-form the index-finger barre slightly ahead of the beat and use open or passing chords on the final eighth-note to pivot smoothly.
